adler.summary: Austrian physician who founded individual psychology and was once an important member of Freud's circle

jung.summary: Swiss psychiatrist who founded analytical psychology; early in his career he worked at the Burghölzli hospital

von-franz.summary: Swiss Jungian analyst who studied fairy tales and alchemy

hillman.summary: American Jungian analyst who founded archetypal psychology

samuels.summary: British Jungian analyst who focuses on analytical psychology in politics and culture

neumann.summary: Israeli Jungian analyst who studied the origins and history of consciousness

fordham.summary: British Jungian analyst who brought infant observation and object relations into analytical psychology

kalff.summary: Swiss Jungian analyst who developed sandplay therapy

kawai.summary: Japanese clinical psychologist who introduced Jungian psychology and sandplay to Japan

pauli.summary: Austrian physicist and Nobel laureate who worked with Jung on synchronicity

klein.summary: Austrian-born British psychoanalyst and a pioneer of child analysis and object relations

winnicott.summary: British pediatrician and psychoanalyst who proposed the holding environment, transitional objects, and the true and false self

horney.summary: German-born American psychoanalyst who criticized Freud's views of women and emphasized culture and interpersonal relations

sullivan.summary: American psychiatrist and founder of interpersonal psychiatry

fromm.summary: German-born American psychoanalyst and social psychologist who combined psychoanalysis with social criticism

lacan.summary: French psychoanalyst who brought structural linguistics into psychoanalysis

kohut.summary: Austrian-born American psychoanalyst and founder of self psychology

mitchell.summary: American psychoanalyst and a leading founder of relational psychoanalysis

benjamin.summary: American psychoanalyst who proposed the theory of mutual recognition

fonagy.summary: Hungarian-born British psychoanalyst and a leading proponent of mentalization theory

bateman.summary: British psychiatrist who developed mentalization-based treatment with Fonagy

witmer.summary: American psychologist who opened the first psychological clinic in 1896 and coined the term "clinical psychology"

kraepelin.summary: German psychiatrist and founder of the modern classification of psychiatric disorders

bleuler.summary: Swiss psychiatrist who introduced the term "schizophrenia" and was Jung's superior

shoma-morita.summary: Japanese psychiatrist and founder of Morita therapy

spitzer.summary: American psychiatrist who led the revision of DSM-III

rosenhan.summary: American psychologist who published the study "On Being Sane in Insane Places"

frances.summary: American psychiatrist who led DSM-IV and later criticized DSM-5 for widening the boundaries of mental disorders

ellis.summary: American psychologist and founder of rational emotive behavior therapy, who had trained in psychoanalysis

beck.summary: American psychiatrist and founder of cognitive therapy, who had trained in psychoanalysis

bateson.summary: English-born American anthropologist who proposed the double bind theory and influenced family systems thinking

bowen.summary: American psychiatrist and founder of family systems theory

minuchin.summary: Argentine-born American psychiatrist and founder of structural family therapy

frank.summary: American psychiatrist, author of "Persuasion and Healing," and a pioneer of common factors research

wampold.summary: American psychologist who proposed a contextual model of psychotherapy

rosenzweig.summary: American psychologist who in 1936 first proposed the "Dodo bird verdict" metaphor

luborsky.summary: American psychologist who studied psychotherapy outcomes and the therapeutic alliance

bordin.summary: American psychologist who proposed the concept of the working alliance

engel.summary: American physician who proposed the biopsychosocial model

zubin.summary: American psychologist who proposed the vulnerability model of schizophrenia

meichenbaum.summary: American psychologist and founder of cognitive behavior modification and stress inoculation training

jacobson.summary: American psychologist who researched behavioral activation

meyer.summary: British clinical psychologist who first reported exposure and response prevention for obsessive-compulsive disorder

clark.summary: British psychologist who proposed cognitive models of panic and social anxiety

kabat-zinn.summary: American medical professor who founded the Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction program

herman.summary: American psychiatrist, author of "Trauma and Recovery," who proposed complex trauma

foa.summary: Israeli-born American psychologist and founder of prolonged exposure therapy

resick.summary: American psychologist and founder of cognitive processing therapy

shapiro.summary: American psychologist and founder of EMDR

van-der-kolk.summary: Dutch-born American psychiatrist, author of "The Body Keeps the Score," who promoted the concept of developmental trauma disorder

levine.summary: American psychologist and founder of Somatic Experiencing

tedeschi.summary: American psychologist who proposed posttraumatic growth with Calhoun

hayes.summary: American psychologist and founder of acceptance and commitment therapy

linehan.summary: American psychologist and founder of dialectical behavior therapy

segal.summary: Canadian psychologist and co-developer of mindfulness-based cognitive therapy

williams-mark.summary: British psychologist and co-developer of mindfulness-based cognitive therapy

teasdale.summary: British psychologist and co-developer of mindfulness-based cognitive therapy

gilbert.summary: British psychologist and founder of compassion-focused therapy

insel.summary: American psychiatrist who directed the National Institute of Mental Health and promoted RDoC

cuthbert.summary: American psychologist and one of the main designers of RDoC

kotov.summary: American psychologist and one of the lead authors of the HiTOP consortium

krueger.summary: American psychologist who studies the dimensional structure of psychopathology and HiTOP

caspi.summary: Israeli-born American psychologist who proposed the p factor and leads the Dunedin longitudinal study

lazarus.summary: American psychologist who proposed the cognitive appraisal theory of stress

folkman.summary: American psychologist who studied stress and coping with Lazarus

rotter.summary: American psychologist who proposed the concept of locus of control and social learning theory

sporns.summary: American neuroscientist at Indiana University who coined the term "human connectome" with colleagues in 2005 and developed methods for brain network analysis

sullivan-patrick.summary: Psychiatric geneticist and lead investigator of the Psychiatric Genomics Consortium (PGC), founded in 2007

schultz.summary: Neuroscientist who recorded dopamine neurons in monkeys and found that their activity matches a "reward prediction error"

sutton.summary: One of the founders of reinforcement learning, who proposed temporal-difference learning and co-wrote "Reinforcement Learning" with Barto

hinton.summary: English-born Canadian computer scientist, trained early in psychology, who has long championed neural networks and deep learning

kosinski.summary: Computational social scientist who studies how digital footprints reveal personality and who has recently tested the "mind" abilities of large language models

borsboom.summary: Dutch psychologist who proposed viewing mental disorders as networks of interacting symptoms

steinberg.summary: American developmental psychologist who studies adolescent risk-taking and proposed a dual-systems model of adolescent brain development

turkheimer.summary: American behavioral geneticist who proposed the three laws of behavioral genetics in 2000

darcy.summary: Psychology researcher and one of the developers of Woebot, a conversational mental health program, and first author of a 2017 trial paper

twenge.summary: American psychologist who studies generational differences and argues that the spread of smartphones is linked to declining adolescent mental health

mcguire.summary: American social psychologist who proposed attitude inoculation theory: exposure to weakened counterarguments can build resistance

lomas.summary: British psychologist who, with Ivtzan, proposed "second-wave positive psychology" and studies the dialectic between positive and negative aspects of well-being

solms.summary: South African neuropsychologist and psychoanalyst and one of the founders of neuropsychoanalysis

shedler.summary: American clinical psychologist who published a 2010 review of the evidence for psychodynamic therapy

barlow.summary: American clinical psychologist who studies anxiety disorders and led the development of a unified transdiagnostic protocol

hofmann.summary: German-born American clinical psychologist who studies cognitive behavioral therapy and social anxiety, and with Hayes advocates process-based therapy

griffiths.summary: American psychopharmacologist at Johns Hopkins University and one of the first researchers to study psilocybin with modern controlled methods

chambless.summary: American clinical psychologist who studies anxiety disorders and was the first author of "The Update of Empirically Validated Therapies" (1998)

hippocrates-of-cos.summary: Ancient Greek physician whose school explained temperament and disease through the four humors

ibn-sina.summary: Persian scholar and physician, author of "The Canon of Medicine"

epictetus.summary: Stoic philosopher who held that it is our judgments about things, not the things themselves, that disturb us

john-locke.summary: English philosopher and leading empiricist who proposed the mind as a blank slate and that ideas are linked through experience

jean-jacques-rousseau.summary: Geneva-born thinker and author of "Emile," who argued that childhood has its own stages and value

franz-mesmer.summary: German physician who proposed "animal magnetism" and is a forerunner of hypnosis research

immanuel-kant.summary: German philosopher who argued that the mind organizes experience using innate categories

philippe-pinel.summary: French physician who advocated "moral treatment" for people with mental illness

franz-gall.summary: German neuroanatomist and founder of phrenology, who held that mental faculties correspond to different brain regions

arthur-schopenhauer.summary: German philosopher who held that people are driven by an unconscious will

adolphe-quetelet.summary: Belgian statistician who applied the normal distribution to human characteristics and proposed the "average man"

soren-kierkegaard.summary: Danish philosopher who understood anxiety as the experience of facing freedom and possibility

hermann-helmholtz.summary: German physicist and physiologist who measured the speed of nerve conduction and was Wundt's teacher

moritz-lazarus.summary: German psychologist who co-founded the journal of folk psychology with Steinthal

isabel-briggs-myers.summary: American writer who, together with her mother, developed the MBTI based on Jung's typology

katharine-briggs.summary: American writer who began developing the MBTI with her daughter after reading Jung's "Psychological Types"

vosoughi.summary: Computer scientist and first author of the 2018 Science study on the spread of true and false news

casey.summary: Developmental cognitive neuroscientist and first author of the imaging acquisition paper for the ABCD study

jennifer-mitchell.summary: Neuroscientist and first author of the phase 3 trial paper on MDMA-assisted therapy for PTSD
